Extract the brain from a 'T1'-weighted image (without 'Python')

Source: R/workflow-yael_brain_extract.R
yael_brain_extract.Rd

The brain mask of a 'T1'-weighted 'MRI', computed in 'R' by the native YAEL engine on top of ravetools: the brain mask of the template 'mni_icbm152_nlin_asym_09a', brought to the image by a registration (or a given initial mask), is adjusted to the subject.

Usage

yael_brain_extract(
  image,
  mask = NULL,
  work_path = NULL,
  affine_transform = NULL,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

image

the 'T1'-weighted image: a file path, an ieegio_volume, or anything else that ieegio::as_ieegio_volume accepts

mask

optional initial brain mask in the same scanner space (the voxels above zero), in the same forms as image; when given, the template and its registration are not used. A mask on another grid, such as a 'FreeSurfer' brainmask.mgz, is resampled onto the grid of image (nearest neighbor)

work_path

folder for the working files, which are kept; default NULL uses a temporary folder that is removed at the end

affine_transform

optional initial affine transform from the template to the image (scanner 'RAS' to scanner 'RAS', the point map of 'ANTs'): an 'ANTs' .mat file or a 4-by-4 matrix; the registration then only runs its non-linear stage. Ignored when mask is given

verbose

whether to log the steps and print the registration progress

Value

A binary ieegio_volume (1 inside the brain) on the grid of image.

Details

The steps, with the files they write into work_path (named after the stages of the native normalization):

  1. bias-field correction with the settings of abp_n4 in 'ANTsPy' (nu.nii.gz), for the registration;

  2. unless mask is given, the registration of the whole head to the template image without masks, affine and then deformable (only deformable from affine_transform), as the initial registration ('SyNabp') of the native normalization; it is saved by ravetools::save_registration as SyNabp.dcf with its 'ANTs' transform files, and the registered image as SyNabp_warped_mov.nii.gz;

  3. the initial mask: the template brain mask through that registration, or mask (initial_mask.nii.gz);

  4. the brain extraction of the native engine (see the item "Brain extraction" of YAELNativeProcess) on the image corrected by N4 again without the intensity truncation of abp_n4 (which makes bright marrow look like the white matter), which keeps the largest connected gray and white matter, leaves out what dark voxels cut off from it (skull marrow, dura or scalp) and thin strands, and keeps the initial mask, with a warning, when the result differs from it by more than 20 percent in volume (brainmask.nii.gz).

Every call computes all the steps again; existing files in work_path are replaced.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

# downloads the template on first use, and takes a few minutes
mask <- yael_brain_extract("sub-01_T1w.nii.gz", work_path = "brain_extraction")
ieegio::write_volume(mask, "sub-01_desc-brain_mask.nii.gz")

# adjust a mask of the same image instead
mask2 <- yael_brain_extract("sub-01_T1w.nii.gz", mask = "fs/mri/brainmask.mgz")

} # }
